name: TwoTrees TTS-55 20W
tagline: 20W Ultra-budget diode with surprising build quality for the price
tldr: TwoTrees TTS-55 20W is the 20W SKU on the TwoTrees twotrees tts 55 line. TwoTrees undercuts Atomstack and Ortur on price while offering a usable 5. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Everyday engraving plus reliable light cutting on wood, leather, and dark acrylic

priceRange.note: 20W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Basswood up to 8 mm in our profile, against 5 mm with the 10W module
About a third faster than the 10W in our benchmark: ~18–28 min for a 10 × 10 cm photo, ~9–15 min for a 3 mm basswood square
TwoTrees still sells the 20W module for the TTS-55 ($359, October 2026), so spares exist
cons: Slower than newer 20W machines: fill speeds of 12–31 mm/s and 2–3 mm/s cuts in our tests
Price spread is very wide ($159–433): listings mix complete machines, bare modules and old stock
200 mm/s frame and 300 × 300 mm bed date from the original TTS-55 design
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on TwoTrees TTS-55. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Use air assist for cuts, lower scan speed for photo engraving. Multiple passes at moderate speed beat one aggressive pass. Check the flagship tier’s cut benchmark if you quote production times to customers.

editorialDepth.advantages: TwoTrees TTS-55 20W is the versatile hobby / side-business SKU: clean engraving and light wood or leather cuts with comparable benchmarks on Maker Atlas.
editorialDepth.limitations: Open-frame: glasses and exhaust required. TwoTrees lists no 40W module for the TTS-55: if cutting takes over, move to a 40W machine. Not a CO₂ replacement for clear acrylic or heavy thick-stock production.

faq.question: What does the 20W module change on the TTS-55?
faq.answer: Mostly cutting depth and time. Our profile moves the basswood limit from 5 mm (10W) to 8 mm, and our benchmark cuts the 3 mm test square in ~9–15 min instead of ~14–24 min. Photo fills drop from ~28–43 min to ~18–28 min.

faq.question: Is a TTS-55 20W a better buy than a newer 20W machine?
faq.answer: Only if it is clearly cheaper. The TTS-55 frame is limited to 200 mm/s and a 300 × 300 mm bed in our profile, and our fill speeds (12–31 mm/s) trail newer 20W designs. At the low end of its $159–433 spread it is good value; near the top, newer machines make more sense.

faq.question: TTS-55 20W or 40W: which one should a buyer pick?
faq.answer: The 20W suits hobbyists who cut up to about 5 mm and engrave regularly. The 40W listings ($349–499) shorten our photo test to ~12–18 min and reach 10 mm basswood, but confirm the module source, since TwoTrees' own store lists 20W modules for the TTS family, not 40W.

standoutFeatures.title: 8 mm basswood on a budget frame
standoutFeatures.body: Our profile lists basswood up to 8 mm with the 20W module, with several passes near the limit.

standoutFeatures.title: Module still sold
standoutFeatures.body: TwoTrees lists the 20W module for the TTS-55 at $359 (October 2026), which keeps repairs possible on an older frame.
